## Discovery report

### Existing components

**Static component**
- **Path:** `src/components/sections/metafi-features.tsx`
- **Suitable for porting:** Yes
- **Notes:**
  - Section: centered label (“Features”), headline, description.
  - Feature cards: array of `{ title, description, image }`. Four cards; layout is two rows of two (first row `flex-1` + `500px`, second row `500px` + `flex-1`).
  - Some cards use fixed animation components by title: “Checkout” → `AnimationCheckout`, “Recurring Billing” → `AnimationRecurringBilling`, “Invoicing” → `AnimationInvoicing`, “Payment Link” → `AnimationPaymentLink`. Others use an image.
  - Styling: `FeatureCard` with rounded card, title, description, and a block that either renders one of the four animations or an `<Image>`.

**Similar cms-components**
- **hero:** Single-level content + optional media; `useLiveUpdates` + `useContentfulInspectorModeProps`; fallbacks and media handling (including LL-008).
- **faq:** Nested collection (`itemsCollection` → `FaqItem`); good pattern for a Features section with many Feature items.
- **tabbed-content:** Nested `itemsCollection` (here as `itemsCollectionCollection` in GraphQL due to field ID); mapper in `page.ts` for raw → fragment.

### Patterns to follow

From **hero**
- Live preview: `useLiveUpdates(data)` and `useContentfulInspectorModeProps(data.sys.id)`.
- Field access: `liveData.fieldName ?? 'fallback'`.
- Media: support both mapped and raw field names (e.g. `image` and `media`) for live updates (LL-008).

From **block-renderer/configs**
- Registration: `typename` must match Contentful `__typename` exactly (e.g. `'Faq'`, `'Tabbedcontent'`).
- Import: `import { Features } from '@/cms-components/features';` and same style for the new block.

From **faq / tabbed-content**
- Nested items: in GraphQL use `itemsCollection` (or `featuresCollection` if the field ID is `features`) with `items { ... }`; in code use `.items` on the collection.
- Mapper in `page.ts`: map raw section → fragment; map each raw item → `FeatureItemFragment` (or equivalent); handle `__typename` from API (e.g. `Faqitem` vs `FaqItem`).

### Applicable lessons

| Lesson | Applies because |
|--------|------------------|
| LL-002 | Block resolution uses `data.__typename`; must match Contentful (e.g. `Features`, `Featureitem`) in types and config. |
| LL-003 | Section has a list of feature cards; use `*Collection { items { ... } }` in query and `.items` in code. |
| LL-006 | Content type names: use spaces (“Feature Item”, “Features”) so API IDs / `__typename` are predictable. |
| LL-007 | Reference field (e.g. `items` or `features`) gets a `Collection` suffix in GraphQL (`itemsCollection` / `featuresCollection`). |
| LL-008 | If we add an image/asset on the feature item, support both mapped and raw field names in the component for live preview. |

### Content-model-proposal reference

`documentation/content-model-proposal.md` already defines:

- **features** section: `internalName`, `variant`, `eyebrow`, `headline`, `subheadline`, `features` (References → feature), `ntExperiences`.
- **feature** item: `title`, `description`, `icon`, `image`, `animationType` (e.g. `checkout`, `invoicing`, `payment-link`, `recurring`).

We’ll align the new block with this and the existing static component (label = eyebrow, headline, description, list of feature cards with title, description, and image or animation).

### Pre–Q&A recommendations

1. **Port from `metafi-features.tsx`:** Keep layout (two rows of two cards) and card styling; drive label, headline, description, and cards from Contentful.
2. **Field IDs:** Use `items` for the references list (so GraphQL is `itemsCollection`) to stay consistent with Faq and avoid double-`Collection` naming (LL-007).
3. **Feature item:** Include `title`, `description`, and `image` (Asset). Optionally add `animationType` (Symbol) so the app can render the same four animations when set; otherwise fall back to `image`.
4. **Personalization:** Add `ntExperiencesCollection` only if you want Ninetailed experiences on this section; otherwise omit for v1.

## Summary

### 1. **No variant**
- Features section has no variant field (label, title, description, items, personalization only).

### 2. **Reusable animation handling**
- **`src/lib/feature-visual-registry.tsx`**  
  - `FEATURE_VISUAL_KEYS`: `'checkout' | 'recurring-billing' | 'invoicing' | 'payment-link'`.  
  - `getFeatureVisualComponent(key)` returns the React component for that key.  
- Any block (or future “Feature Item” usage) can use the same keys; new keys can be added in this file.

### 3. **Flexible 2–4 (or 1) feature layout**
- **`src/cms-components/features/features.tsx`**  
  - Uses a responsive grid: 1 column by default, 2 columns on `lg`.  
  - 1 item: single column, centered, `max-w-2xl`.  
  - 2–4 items: same grid; cards flow in order (no fixed “row 1 = 2, row 2 = 2”).

### 4. **Personalization**
- **Fragment:** `FeaturesFragment` includes `ntExperiencesCollection?: { items: Array<...> }`.  
- **Query:** `FEATURES_FIELDS` requests `ntExperiencesCollection(limit: 10) { items { __typename sys { id } } }`.  
- **Mapper:** `mapFeatures` passes `ntExperiencesCollection` through.  
- **Component:** Does not render experiences; data is there for when you connect the personalization app.

### 5. **Content model (for when you create in Contentful)**
- **Features:** internalName, **label**, **title**, **description**, **items** (References → Feature Item), **ntExperiences** (References → NtExperience).

- Use field ID **`items`** (so GraphQL is `itemsCollection` per LL-007).

Summary of what was wrong and what was changed:

**Cause of the 404**  
The page failed because the GraphQL request returned **400**. The API reported:  
`Unknown type "Featureitem". Did you mean "FeatureItem"?`  
So the query was using the wrong type name for the Feature Item content type.

**Change made**  
Contentful’s content type ID is `featureItem` (camelCase), and the GraphQL type name is **`FeatureItem`** (capital I), not `Featureitem`.

1. **`src/services/contentful/queries.ts`**  
   In the fragment, `... on Featureitem {` was updated to `... on FeatureItem {`.

2. **`src/services/contentful/page.ts`**  
   The mapper was updated so it checks for the typename returned by the API: `item.__typename !== 'Featureitem'` → `item.__typename !== 'FeatureItem'`.

Summary:

---

**Log analysis (evidence)**

From the latest run (e.g. line 4 in `debug.log`):

- **featuresItemsCount: 4** – Features section has 4 items
- **hasItemsCollection: true** – Items are present
- **mappedCount: 4**, **hasFeatures: true** – All 4 sections (Hero, Faq, TabbedContent, Features) are returned and mapped

So when the app serves `/page/kaz-test`, it receives the Features section and all four feature items from GraphQL and passes them through to the page. There is no backend bug here.

---

**Conclusion**

The “features reference is not showing anything” is **not** due to the Next.js app. The app is returning the correct data.

Likely causes:

1. **Contentful preview URL** – The preview URL configured for the Page content type in Contentful (Settings → Content preview) might not point at your app’s page URL (e.g. `https://your-domain/page/kaz-test` or `http://localhost:3000/page/kaz-test`). If the iframe loads the wrong URL, you won’t see the sections your app is rendering.
2. **Contentful “sections” field UI** – The “+ Add content” area in the sidebar is how Contentful shows the **sections** reference field. If the 4 entries (Hero, FAQ, TabbedContent, Features) are linked in the API but not visible in that widget, that’s a Contentful UI/configuration issue (e.g. reference editor type or field settings).

**What to do**

- **To see Features on your site:** Open `http://localhost:3000/page/kaz-test` (or your deployed URL) in the browser. You should see Hero, FAQ, TabbedContent, and Features with 4 cards.
- **To fix the preview iframe:** In Contentful, set the Page preview URL to your app URL plus the page path, e.g. `https://your-app.com/page/{{entry.fields.slug}}` (or the slug for this page, e.g. `kaz-test`), so the iframe loads the same route the app uses.
- **To fix the “sections” list in the editor:** Check the Page content type’s “sections” field in Contentful: widget type (e.g. “Reference” / “Multiple references”) and that it’s set to show the list of linked entries. If links are saved but not shown, it’s a Contentful UI/config issue.

Debug instrumentation has been removed from `page.ts`. No code change was required for data loading; the issue is in Contentful configuration or preview URL, not in the app code.

If it’s by slug, the app may be using a cached or non-preview response for that URL, so section changes in the editor wouldn’t show until publish/refresh. Making this explicit helps narrow the fix (e.g. ensure draft mode + preview API and no caching for that route).

2. **One concrete scenario** – Picking one scenario (e.g. “reorder two sections in Sections, save draft, expect preview to update within X seconds”) and stating it as the primary test case would make success easier to verify.

Summary of what was implemented:

---

**1. No hardcoding**  
Sections (including Features) come only from Contentful. The page is loaded by slug via `getPageBySlug`; the list of sections is the Page entry’s `sections` field. Nothing is hardcoded.

**2. Why preview didn’t update**  
The page was rendered once on the server. There was no subscription to the **Page** entry, so changes to the Page’s sections (add/remove/reorder) in the editor didn’t trigger a refetch or re-render. Individual blocks (Hero, Features, etc.) use `useLiveUpdates` for their own fields, but the **list** of sections is owned by the Page entry, so it wasn’t updating.

**3. Changes made**

- **Page identity for live preview**  
  - `PAGE_BY_SLUG` now requests `__typename` and `sys { id }` for the page.  
  - `getPageBySlug` returns `sys: { id }` on the page payload.  
  - `PageData` includes optional `sys?: { id: string }`.

- **Client wrapper with live updates**  
  - **`src/app/page/[slug]/page-content-live.tsx`** (new):  
    - Takes `page` from the server.  
    - Uses `useLiveUpdates(page)` so field-level edits on the page can update.  
    - Calls `ContentfulLivePreview.subscribe('edit', { data: page, locale: 'en-US', callback: () => router.refresh() })` so **any** edit on the Page entry (including sections add/remove/reorder) triggers a server refetch and re-render.

- **Page route**  
  - **`src/app/page/[slug]/page.tsx`** now renders `<PageContentLive page={page} />` instead of mapping sections directly, so all page views (including preview) go through the live-update + refresh logic.

**4. Result**  
When you change, reorder, add, or remove section references in the Page’s “Sections” field in Contentful (draft, no publish), the preview iframe should update after the subscription callback runs and `router.refresh()` refetches the page.

---

**How to verify**

1. Restart dev server: `bun run dev`.
2. Open the kaz-test page in live preview (your Contentful preview URL).
3. In the editor, reorder two sections (e.g. drag Features above FAQ), or add/remove a section reference.  
   The preview should update without publishing or manually refreshing.

**Screenshots (contentful debug skill)**  
The contentful-live-preview-verify skill uses agent-browser to capture console, network, and a screenshot. To get before/after screenshots of section reordering, you can run it (or use the browser) once with the original section order, then change the order in Contentful and run/capture again to confirm the preview matches the new order.

Summary of the comparison and what’s in place:

**Comparison with the other agent’s findings**

- **Demo 2.0 (colorful-demo-2.0-1):** No page-level `subscribe('edit')` or `subscribe('save')`; only `useContentfulLiveUpdates` in components for field-level updates. So demo 2.0 does **not** refetch the full page when section references change.
- **Contentful docs:** The “no client components” pattern uses `subscribe('save', { callback })` and then revalidate/reload to pick up structural/reference changes.
- **This repo (before):** Only `subscribe('edit')` in `page-content-live.tsx`, so add/remove/reorder of sections didn’t refresh until publish + reload.

**Implemented change**

- In `page-content-live.tsx`, a second subscription was added for `'save'` that also calls `router.refresh()`:
  - **`edit`** — still used for field-level ENTRY_UPDATED; refresh keeps behavior consistent.
  - **`save`** — ENTRY_SAVED when the user saves the entry; refresh after save picks up section reference changes (add/remove/reorder) without publishing.

The SDK type is `subscribe(event: 'save', config: Pick<ContentfulSubscribeConfig, 'callback'>): VoidFunction`, so `subscribe('save', { callback: () => router.refresh() })` is correct. The save event is global (no payload), so any save in the editor will trigger a refresh; that’s the same tradeoff as in the docs.

**TASKS.md**

- The “Live preview: refreshing when section references change” section now has an **Implemented** line and a short manual test step (change sections, save without publishing, confirm iframe updates).

**What you should do**

1. In Contentful, open a Page in the editor and change sections (add/remove/reorder).
2. Save the entry (do not publish).
3. Confirm the preview iframe updates to show the new section list. If it does, we can treat this as fixed and remove any temporary debug logging. If not, we can add logging or a more targeted subscription next.

**What’s in place**

2. **TASKS.md** updated with the current hypothesis and what to check next.

**How to get runtime evidence**

1. **Open the preview iframe’s console**  
   In Chrome: open DevTools (F12 or Cmd+Option+I) → at the top of the Console there’s a frame/context dropdown (often “top”) → switch it to the **iframe** that shows your app (e.g. `http://localhost:3000/page/...`). All `[PageContentLive]` logs appear in that iframe’s context.

2. **Reproduce:**
   - In Contentful, open a **Page** entry and use **Live preview** so the iframe loads your app.

     - **(B)** Do you see `[PageContentLive] save callback → router.refresh()`?
     - **(C)** Does the iframe content actually update (e.g. Features block appears)?

3. **Report back:**
   - If you see **(A)** but not **(B)** → the message reaches the iframe but the SDK isn’t calling our save callback (e.g. init/registration issue).

Once you have (A/B/C) from one run, we can decide the next fix (e.g. poll on visibility, manual “Refresh preview” button, or fixing init/subscription so the save callback runs).

  `key={\`${section.sys.id}-${index}\`}`  
  This removes the duplicate-key warning when the same section reference is used multiple times.

Summary of what was fixed and how to verify it:

---

**Root cause**

With **inspector mode** on, the Contentful Live Preview SDK only runs the **save** callback when the saved entry’s ID is in the **tagged** list (entries that have `getProps()` in the page). The **Page** entry itself is not tagged (only the section blocks are), so when you saved the Page after reordering sections, the SDK never called our callback and we never ran `router.refresh()`.

**Fix**

In `page-content-live.tsx` we now handle **ENTRY_SAVED** ourselves via `postMessage` and only react when the saved entry is the current page:

- Listen for `message` with `e.data.method === 'ENTRY_SAVED'`.
- If `e.data.entity?.sys?.id === page.sys.id`, call `router.refresh()`.

This runs regardless of inspector mode. The SDK `subscribe('save')` is still there for environments where the callback does run.

**Verification (agent-browser)**

1. Opened Contentful kaz-test entry and Live Preview.
2. Refreshed the preview so the iframe loaded the new code.
3. Triggered a save from the editor (small edit + autosave).
4. In the **iframe** console we saw:
   - `[PageContentLive] ENTRY_SAVED { entityId: 6yuInMRWMJc5kKiFtW4gea, pageId: 6yuInMRWMJc5kKiFtW4gea, match: true }`
   - `[PageContentLive] ENTRY_SAVED for this page → router.refresh()`

So the handler runs and calls `router.refresh()` when you save the current page.

**Files updated**

- `src/app/page/[slug]/page-content-live.tsx` – ENTRY_SAVED `postMessage` handler that calls `router.refresh()` when the saved entity is this page; dev log for `entityId` / `pageId` / `match`.
- `.cursor/live-preview-diagnostic-report.md` – root cause and fix notes.
- `TASKS.md` – same notes.

**Reproduction steps (to confirm real-time update)**

1. Restart dev server so the latest code is running (`bun run dev`).
2. In Contentful, open the kaz-test Page entry and open **Live Preview**.
3. Reorder sections (e.g. drag Features above Faq) or add/remove a section.
4. Save (autosave or explicit save).
5. Check the preview iframe: it should update without using “Refresh preview” or publishing. In the iframe console you should see `ENTRY_SAVED for this page → router.refresh()` when you save.

If the iframe still doesn’t update after save, the next place to look is whether `router.refresh()` is refetching draft data (e.g. RSC cache or draft cookie on the refetch). In that case we can try calling `window.location.reload()` when we get ENTRY_SAVED for this page so the preview always shows the latest after a full reload.
